locator.text: Equation (6.26), p. 70, in the statement of Proposition 6.6

evidence: paper: M_*(Z,T) := \int R^e \langle f_*\rangle_Y \, dR = Q^{\,a_f - (e+1)/2} \int r^e \langle f_{\mathrm{phys}}\rangle_Y \, dr .

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's single display is split across the repository into its two halves, and no declaration was found that states both at once. The defining half, M_*(Z,T) = ∫ R^e ⟨f_*⟩_Y dR, is pressureMass_radialWeighted: pressureMass of the radially weighted field equals radialMoment e of the torus average, and radialMoment/moment unfold to ∫ r^e F(r,p). The scaling half is nativeSource_mass with lengthScale q p = √(q p): rewriting the radius by R = r/√Q multiplies the e-th radial moment by √Q^{-(e+1)} = Q^{-(e+1)/2}, which is exactly the Lean's `mass e F p / lengthScale q p ^ (e + 1)`; the remaining factor Q^{a_f} comes from the paper's normalisation f_* = Q^{a_f} f_phys, pulled out of the integral by moment_const_mul, and the torus average commutes with the radial dilation because the dilation acts only on the first coordinate. Composing these gives (6.26). The composition is three rewrites and was not found as one lemma; RenormalizedHeatMoment.physical_moment_scaling (NavierStokes/RenormalizedHeatMoment.lean:344) states the scaling only for e = 2, so the general-e statement rests on nativeSource_mass, which is general in e. Packaging, not a mathematical difference.
